auditor_value: T = 4(1 + 1/√3) ≈ 6.31 s; range down the slope = 160/√3 + 160/3 ≈ 145.7 m (velocity at 75° to the incline, thrown downhill)

findings.note: The step's text says the range is the along-incline distance covered in time T with gravity's along-incline part adding, but the equation only restates the results; the along-incline equation that produces 145.71 m is never written, so a student cannot follow how R was obtained.

notes: Re-computed in ground axes (x = 20t, y = 20t − 5t² meeting y = −x tan30°): t = 6.309 s, x = 126.19 m, R = x/cos30° = 145.71 m; incline axes agree (T = 2u sin75°/(g cos30°) = 6.309 s; R = 7.32·6.31 + 2.5·39.8 = 145.7 m). Exact forms 4(3+√3)/3 and 160(√3+1)/3 verified. Mistake entries verified: 15° to incline gives 1.69 s / 39.04 m; flat ground gives 4 s / 80 m.
